speaker: Mr Fadli Fawzi
text: And lastly, it would be good for this House to reflect on why is it that this happened.

speaker: Mr Fadli Fawzi
text: So, I would also like to reiterate my last question on whether a cross-Government review has been commissioned in response to the discovery, because if it has happened for such a routine manner for over a long period of time, one can easily think or suspect that it may recur in other areas, so that we can nip this problem in the bud early.

speaker: Dr Syed Harun Alhabsyi
text: First of all, it is important that we frame this Bill amendment appropriately.

speaker: Dr Syed Harun Alhabsyi
text: The Member frames it as having those affected, whereby it seems to suggest that there was a mistake made in the past and therefore we are trying to correct it; and something that we have done in the past seem to be egregious in that sense.

speaker: Dr Syed Harun Alhabsyi
text: But the spirit of this Bill is really about making sure that we move forward with the legislative backing and mandate for our agencies.

speaker: Dr Syed Harun Alhabsyi
text: Previously, these everyday charges, with regard to allowing the four agencies to fulfil their statutory functions, were regarded as administrative charges.

speaker: Dr Syed Harun Alhabsyi
text: And services were indeed duly provided by the agencies, and tomorrow, services will still be provided for by the agencies.

speaker: Mr Fadli Fawzi
text: I just would like to make it clear.

speaker: Mr Fadli Fawzi
text: I have no problems going forward about regularising such provisions.

speaker: Mr Fadli Fawzi
text: My concern is that we have no idea about the actual numbers that are being involved and we are asked to extinguish the rights of these people to claim any monies.

speaker: Mr Fadli Fawzi
text: So, would the Ministry agree with me that the numbers are important, especially when assessing the risk of any oversight that has occurred with regard to the regulation of this Bill?

speaker: Dr Syed Harun Alhabsyi
text: The fees were openly prescribed to the extent to where the services were required by Singaporeans, as well as consumers.

speaker: Dr Syed Harun Alhabsyi
text: And therefore, to that end, the services were indeed duly provided for by the agencies, and on top of that, it was on the basis of cost recovery.

speaker: Dr Syed Harun Alhabsyi
text: I hope that reassures the Member that whatever fees that were rendered were indeed transacted appropriately through the different agencies, in accordance with their desire to make sure that the services were rendered for the public good, as well as that of the industry.

speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
text: I have one clarification for the Senior Parliamentary Secretary, and that is on the necessity for the retrospective legislation.

speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
text: Because if I heard him correctly in his opening speech, he said that there was a comprehensive internal review, after which MND was advised that the fees and charges should have been prescribed in the legislation – should have been prescribed.

speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
text: But in his round-up speech, he appears to be shifting to say that MND was advised that it is better to do it.

speaker: Dr Syed Harun Alhabsyi
text: It should have been prescribed and therefore, it was better that it would have been in legislation.

speaker: Mr Speaker
text: Ms Sylvia Lim, if you like to respond —

speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim
text: On that clarification, then, we are given to understand that the collections were actually not legally authorised.

speaker: Dr Syed Harun Alhabsyi
text: The fees, which were previously considered as administrative charges, it has been advised to MND to ensure, moving forward, requires legislative backing to continue.

speaker: Dr Syed Harun Alhabsyi
text: Because it is in the service of the statutory functions of the four agencies that are part of this amendment.

speaker: Mr Low Wu Yang Andre
text: My questions to the Senior Parliamentary Secretary are in three parts.

speaker: Mr Low Wu Yang Andre
text: The first is a bit of a repetition of what my colleague, Mr Fawzi previously asked; but I do not believe his clarifications have been adequately addressed.

speaker: Mr Low Wu Yang Andre
text: Second, on the nature of the fees collected, I think my colleague, Ms Sylvia Lim has also alluded to this.

speaker: Mr Low Wu Yang Andre
text: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary mentioned earlier that fees and charges should have been prescribed in legislation – "should have been" being operative term.

speaker: Mr Low Wu Yang Andre
text: On a reading of the fact that this Bill is before us today, that we are regularising the position prospectively, it goes to follow logically that previously, it was not legal.

speaker: Mr Low Wu Yang Andre
text: If there are not going to be any refunds, why no refunds?

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Chee Hong Tat)
text: And he also explained why services were provided and these fees were collected on a cost recovery basis, which is the correct principle.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Chee Hong Tat)
text: So, if the Workers' Party agrees that that is the correct approach – where we provide service, we should recover the cost, which would otherwise have to be funded by taxpayers if we do not do that – then there is really no refund to talk about.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Chee Hong Tat)
text: So, I think that is the first point we go to be clear about.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Chee Hong Tat)
text: The second point is, we did this review ourselves together with the AGC.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Chee Hong Tat)
text: It was not due to a complaint or a question posed by a Member of Parliament.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Chee Hong Tat)
text: We initiated this review and we decided that, to be upfront, to be open, to be transparent, we want to bring it to the House and do it properly.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Chee Hong Tat)
text: Going forward, we want to make sure that we put it into legislation so that there is clarity.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Chee Hong Tat)
text: And for those fees that were collected in the past, and as I have explained, not wrongly collected – they were appropriate and they were correctly collected.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Chee Hong Tat)
text: We want to make sure that we validate and we do this through this Bill.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Chee Hong Tat)
text: So, I hope we understand what this debate is about and what it is not about.

speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
text: Minister, do you have the number of people affected and the quantum of monies we are talking about?

speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
text: Does the Government have that information and is it prepared to share that information in Parliament, before we vote on the Bill?

speaker: Dr Syed Harun Alhabsyi
text: But I can give him some indication in terms of what are the current numbers that we are looking at for specific agencies.

speaker: Dr Syed Harun Alhabsyi
text: We have other administrative fees, which are also levied.

speaker: Dr Syed Harun Alhabsyi
text: But in in total, specific to HDB, as an example, the total annual amount collected — Give me a minute just to make sure my numbers are right.

text: Senior Parliamentary Secretary Dr Syed Harun, do you need more time to gather the numbers?

speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
text: So, we may not have the full accurate record of all the amounts collected that we are able to share with them precisely.

speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
text: And that is why my colleague Senior Parliamentary Secretary Syed Harun was struggling a little bit to look for the exact information.

speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
text: If we agree that that amount that was collected is not incorrect, inappropriate and wrongly collected, but it is because it was regarded as an administrative fee that was charged, then I think whatever that amount is – and we will certainly try our very best to see whether we can arrive at that number accurately – whatever the amount is, it is something which we are trying to do what is right going forward, validating the past collections and going forward, putting it into legislation.

speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
text: So, I do seek Mr Singh's understanding that we are dealing with a situation which goes back decades, and it is not the last three years or the last five years, that we are able to obtain the information easily and accurately.

speaker: Mr Pritam Singh
text: I am also sure the Minister has understood where the Workers' Party Members of Parliament are coming from.

speaker: Mr Pritam Singh
text: And I also would like to add that as the Opposition, we come to this House to scrutinise Bills and it is our duty to ask those questions.

speaker: Mr Pritam Singh
text: Hence, those questions were asked not once, but they were asked repeatedly, I believe.

speaker: Mr Pritam Singh
text: Hence, we had to put that question out, even though I accept what the Minister is saying in terms of how far back it goes – like in the Explanatory Statement to the Bill, we did not know that these charges went back to Independence.

speaker: Mr Pritam Singh
text: So, this is where we have to ask those questions – or some of them, I beg your pardon.

speaker: Mr Pritam Singh
text: And I hope that the Senior Parliamentary Secretary and the Minister have also understood the arguments that have been mounted by the Workers' Party Members of Parliament.

speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
text: I also understand, certainly, where the Workers' Party is coming from.

speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
text: I think it is correct that we be clear what we are putting before the House.

speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
text: And that is why we took effort to explain what this issue is, what is the objective, what are the steps that we are taking, in an open and transparent way.

speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
text: That is something that will be helpful for people to understand.

speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
text: So, if we are able to come up with the information subsequently, to the best of our ability, I think we will certainly be happy to share this with Mr Singh and with the House.

text: But for today, I do seek the support of Members from the Workers' Party that if they agree with the intent of what we are trying to do with this Bill, not just this provision, but the others as well, and the spirit of what we are trying to achieve and the explanations that we have given in terms of what happened, the nature of these fees, what steps we are taking going forward, I do hope to have their support too for this Bill.

text: And in cases where indeed that mistake was made and the wrong collection happened, I think that is the correct thing to do.

speaker: Mr Fadli Fawzi

speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat

speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
text: So, I hope the Workers' Party Members could also agree with our explanation.

speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
text: If we could seek your support for this Bill based on the explanations that we have given, and as I had said earlier, we will go back and see to what extent is possible for us to put together the data that you have requested, we will try our best.

text: If this issue affects a large number of people, there is a larger chance that a mistake would be made.

speaker: Mr Fadli Fawzi
text: That is what I mean by administrative oversight.

speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
text: I think we are talking about two separate things.

speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
text: That is why I said I do not think this is an issue of administrative oversight, in a way which Mr Fadli had described.

speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim
text: I think it is quite clear that we are not denying that services were provided and residents had benefited from the services.

speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim
text: I also would say that we do appreciate that MND did this internal review to undercover this problem, if I can say that.

speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim
text: But would the Minister also not agree really that it is an important safeguard for citizens that the Government acts in accordance with its legal authority?

speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim
text: And one of those principles is that if the Government is going to collect money like taxes, fees from the citizens, then it has to be properly authorised by Parliament?

speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim
text: The fact of the matter is that those past collections were not authorised, and that is why AGC has said that they should have been prescribed.

speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
text: Please allow me to clarify Ms Lim's point.

speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
text: It depends on how the fees are being classified.

speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
text: In this case, they are considered regulatory, and therefore, the advice is that it is more appropriate, it is better if we put it into legislation going forward.

speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
text: I think that is an important point that I need to clarify.

speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
text: It is not that for these administrative fees, we are unauthorised to collect.

speaker: Mr Pritam Singh
text: Minister, I do not want to belabour the question.

speaker: Mr Pritam Singh
text: Was MND advised, after the review with AGC, was it the AGC's position that collections before the First Reading of the Bill were illegal?

speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
text: But AGC also supported – we would not be able to present this Bill if it is not with the support of the AGC – that we come to Parliament and seek Parliament's approval for the Bill to validate the past collections.

speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
text: We do not want to leave this loose end unaddressed about the past collections.

speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
text: Because they were treated as administrative fees in the past – not that they were illegal or inappropriate or wrongly collected, as a few Members have used those terms.

speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
text: But for avoidance of doubt and to reduce ambiguity, it is better to bring it before the House and to validate these fees through this Bill.

speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
text: That is the approach that we are taking.

speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
text: So, we will be in compliance with the advice from AGC, arising from the review.
